item.title: Buddy Red Brings Lil Wayne-Assisted Debut To Kansas City’s Historic Boone Theater
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Buddy Red heads to Kansas City's Boone Theater with a Lil Wayne feature on debut EP Bad News and an open jam for local musicians.
item.content:encoded:
Buddy Red is taking his blues guitar to Kansas City’s historic Boone Theater for his first show in the city on Saturday, November 21.

The Atlanta musician and son of T.I. has Lil Wayne on the title track of his debut studio EP, Bad News, due Friday, November 20.

Before that Boone Theater concert, Red is giving Kansas City musicians a chance to play with him.

Vine Street Brewing Co. is asking people to bring instruments to Friday’s open jam, where proceeds from suggested donations benefit Show Me You Care KC and Castle Studios.

The Saturday bill includes The Phantastics, Noah Francis and Jolson and The Fear of Snakes, The Pitch reported.

The Boone reopened in May after years out of use, returning a former movie and vaudeville house to the city’s 18th & Vine Jazz District. Named for Black concert pianist John “Blind” Boone, it now houses the Black Movie Hall of Fame.

Red didn’t start out trying to play rock shows. He told The Pitch he was making beats at 16, hoping Kendrick Lamar or J. Cole would use one.

Two years later, watching Queen perform in Bohemian Rhapsody made him want to get onstage with an instrument of his own.

“I’m pretty sure that same week I went out and bought my first guitar before I even knew how to properly hold it,” Red said.

He has since made playing multiple instruments part of his recording process. In an interview with Rock and Roll Globe, he broke down his work on “Sexy”: “That’s me playing drums on Sexy! Bass and Guitar too! But I still felt like something was missing.”

Fellow guitarist David Ryan Harris helped him find a direction for the track.

On another Bad News cut, “Sold His Soul,” the starting point was a conversation with his brother about the music business, as Red discussed with Radio Milwaukee.

AllHipHop covered his first stage outing in 2022. This year, he turned his set at Stubb’s during SXSW into a live release.

The Boone lists Saturday’s show for 7 p.m. local time, with general admission at $20 in advance and $25 at the door.

item.title: Nick Cannon Asks For Prayers From A Hospital Bed
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Nick Cannon asks fans for prayers in a photo from a hospital bed and mentions lupus without explaining why he is there.
item.content:encoded:
Nick Cannon used a photo from a hospital bed to ask fans for prayers on Friday.

“This [world] can definitely take a lot out of you! Pray for me y’all,” he wrote over the photo in an Instagram reel. The Wild ‘N Out creator wore a face mask and used “#LupusWarrior” in the caption.

Cannon set the reel to Donny Hathaway’s “A Song for You.” He shared a separate clip of a CT scan to his Instagram Stories. A voice asked if he’d had a CT scan before, but Cannon didn’t say why he was in the hospital.

Cannon’s account of his first symptoms goes back to a hospital stay in Aspen at the beginning of 2012.

He recalled in an interview with WebMD that he’d felt tired and had swelling in his knees before doctors realized his kidneys were failing. “I don’t necessarily look sick, but there are times when I wake up and I can’t move,” Cannon said.

Cannon used his own camera to show what he was dealing with as he returned to work. His NCredible Health Hustle web series followed that stretch, including his decision to step away from his New York morning radio show.

He later made a public service announcement with the Lupus Foundation of America and served as grand marshal at its Washington, D.C., walk.

Cannon was filming Wild ‘N Out when he talked to WebMD about changing his work schedule.

The creator started the MTV show in 2005 and was still taking it on the road two decades later, he told Us Weekly in an interview, adding that he structures his days around rest and twice-daily workouts.

“I work out to stay alive. It’s a challenge, but I’m built for it,” Cannon said.

The rapper and actor has spent the years since that first hospital stay moving between improv, radio and network TV. He went from hosting America’s Got Talent to fronting The Masked Singer, and brought Nick Cannon @ Night to BET for a 10-episode run this year.

Netflix plans to release all eight episodes of Cannon’s new series Raising the Cannons on December 18.

item.title: Molly Santana Plans Headlining Tour After North West Run Falls Through
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Molly Santana says she will headline her next tour after a shelved run with North West, as Black Punk heads for Black Friday.
item.content:encoded:
Molly Santana says she’s going back on the road as a headliner after her planned tour with North West fell through.

She confirmed the new run when Bootleg Kev asked if she’d perform live after Black Punk comes out.

“Yeah. So, tour’s coming,” Santana said. She confirmed she would headline, but didn’t name cities, give a start date or say who would join her.

It’s a different setup from the one she had planned for August. AllHipHop previously reported that Santana and West were booked to co-headline the nine-city Kimokawaii Tour before it was shelved without a public explanation.

Santana didn’t explain that cancellation in the exchange about her new run.

She’s also bringing a different album to the road. Santana said Black Punk is coming on Black Friday, November 27, and explained that the record was supposed to arrive sooner.

She said sample clearances and approvals took more time than on her last album. She described the extra work as part of trying new approaches on the record.

Santana said “certain things happen and certain samples do or don’t happen.” She didn’t name the recordings she was trying to clear or say which ones made the final album.

Black Punk is her first full-length project through her Epic Records partnership with her own Black Punk Music imprint.

The first single under the deal, “A Girl Is a Gun,” came out November 6. Before that, she landed her first Hot 100 entry alongside Drake and Future on “Ran to Atlanta,” which debuted at No. 2.

Santana said the new album has more guest appearances than any of her previous projects.

She declined to name them in the interview, and described how she approached the sessions: “I don’t like making the same stuff.”

The headlining run will put Santana in a different slot than the one she held on Don Toliver’s 2024 Psycho Tour, when she said she first took the stage on a bill with multiple openers. The tour also featured Monaleo and Ski Mask the Slump God.

Bootleg Kev noted that opening first meant performing as fans arrived, describing the slot as a learning experience.

item.title: Looze Cannon Reveals Childhood Record Deal Before Big Michael Fame
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Looze Cannon revisits his childhood label experience and factory work as Big Michael's success brings fresh industry interest.
item.content:encoded:
Looze Cannon‘s first record deal came at 8, but the artist behind “Big Michael Michael” isn’t rushing to sign another one.

In an interview with 97.9 The Beat, the Detroit rapper traced his caution to a childhood deal with Universal. According to the station’s account, the label dropped him after his first album without explaining why.

He kept performing, including work as a rapping birthday clown, before taking a job at a Chrysler plant. Later, he left that job and spent years making content from his basement.

Now that labels are calling again, Cannon favors private investors and keeping control of his work, the station reported. He connected that approach to building something for his young son.

The interview also describes DDG’s advice as a turning point in his move to TikTok, where his comedy and freestyle performances found a bigger audience.

“I just fight negative with positive, you know, and that’s all,” Cannon told the station. “I never like to exchange the same energy.”

His current success has brought attention to recordings that existed before his Michael Jackson-inspired character caught on. His catalog includes Looze Minded, released in 2016, Lil Glen from 2020 and 2023’s Now Or Never. Looze Minded contains 12 tracks across 41 minutes.

Before putting “Big Michael Michael” on streaming services, Cannon offered it as a $1.99 download directly to listeners. AllHipHop previously reported that the record’s growth eventually persuaded him to widen its availability beyond that sales model.

He has also been recording with Eric Bellinger and Roscoe Dash while preparing another project. His recordings also include the 2024 single “Hide & Seek” and an appearance on Melody Renee’s “Beautiful Noise.”

Cannon’s official website describes a career that includes production, DJ work and acting alongside his online performances. It credits the “Big Michael Michael” song’s beginnings to a freestyle during a TikTok livestream.

The site also identifies Beautiful Noise as his first starring role in an independent drama. His long-term goals include stand-up comedy, with Jamie Foxx and Martin Lawrence among the performers he names as models.

Cannon is also working on collaborations with producer Drummerboy, according to his official website.

item.title: Vic Mensa Skips Old Lyrics That No Longer Fit Him
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Vic Mensa explains why he leaves some old Innanetape lyrics unsaid as the mixtape returns to streaming and the stage.
item.content:encoded:
Vic Mensa doesn’t rap every old line the same way anymore, even as he celebrates the music that helped introduce him to listeners.

The Chicago artist said revisiting Innanetape has brought both pride and moments when he stops short of repeating a lyric that no longer fits him.

In an interview with The FADER, Mensa explained that his connection to the mixtape varies from song to song.

He said, “some of this I got to pause and not say that part of the rap, because that doesn’t really match the moment anymore.”

Mensa didn’t name the lines he leaves out. He singled out “Holy Holy” as a song he still feels fully connected to, saying performing it reminds him how much he accomplished while still in high school.

He said some performances still surprise him, particularly when he considers how young he was when he wrote the material.

The recent shows also let him return to the live musicianship at the project’s core. Mensa said playing jazz clubs with a band was a highlight of bringing the mixtape back to the stage.

Originally released in 2013, Innanetape reached streaming services on September 30, giving listeners a simpler way to revisit the project. Its return came ahead of a new full-length album expected in 2027.

The reissue was the first release under Mensa’s partnership with UnitedMasters, announced in September. The arrangement extends beyond recorded music into film, media and commerce while allowing him to retain ownership.

Before that deal, he released sundiata independently through his own website in June.

The anniversary run included an October 28 stop at Garcia’s in Chicago’s West Loop. Chance The Rapper joined him for “Suitcase,” a bonus track on the streaming edition, while Joey Purp opened the show.

Mensa is also working toward a different role on his next album. As AllHipHop previously reported, he described taking himself more seriously as a producer and using voice memos to capture ideas before developing them.

The Vic Mensa Show was announced in August with 24 episodes planned for its first season and Chance The Rapper booked as the premiere guest.

item.title: Jodeci Opens Baltimore’s Paramount With Its First Concert
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jodeci gives Baltimore's new Paramount its first night of live music as the group celebrates 35 years of Forever My Lady.
item.content:encoded:
Jodeci is set to play the first concert at The Paramount Baltimore on Friday, Nov. 20. South Baltimore gets a new music venue, and the first act through the doors will be a group celebrating 35 years of Forever My Lady.

The show is scheduled for 8 p.m. at 555 West Ostend Street, with doors opening an hour earlier, according to the venue. The Paramount sits near M&T Bank Stadium. The venue directs drivers to paid parking next door at Horseshoe Casino and lists light rail and bus service for people coming without a car.

Co-owners Brian Doyle and Bob Goldstein took reporters through the building ahead of opening night, The Baltimore Sun reported through FOX45. The state’s Department of Commerce put a $4 million repayable loan into the 88,000-square-foot project, which includes a radio studio as well as the concert hall.

“Building a first-class entertainment venue in Baltimore has been a dream of mine since I was a kid,” Goldstein told the Maryland Department of Commerce.

K-Ci and JoJo sang gospel in Baltimore long before Jodeci. After moving to the city, they and their father formed Little Cedric and the Hailey Singers.

Jodeci’s debut reached No. 1 on Billboard’s R&B albums chart in 1991. The title song, “Stay” and “Come & Talk To Me” all made it to the top of Billboard’s R&B singles chart. Before it became the name of the album, “Forever My Lady” was on an early demo.

“We knew we had something special, we just didn’t know how special it was,” Mr. Dalvin said in an interview with Mina SayWhat. He said the group now hears younger people sing the words back, after samples and social media put the songs in front of listeners who weren’t around when they first came out.

Baltimore is one stop on the anniversary tour, which has a pair of December dates in Charlotte and a rescheduled Ontario, California, concert in January. The anniversary edition adds five tracks to the debut, including a version of “Stay” that leaves out the instruments and puts the harmonies on their own.

The Paramount’s calendar has another R&B date on Feb. 11, when Baltimore’s own Dru Hill is scheduled to play the room.

item.title: Jill Scott Signs With Independent Artist Group After Five Grammy Nods
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jill Scott signs with Independent Artist Group for film, TV, branding, literary work and international touring.
item.content:encoded:
Jill Scott has signed with Independent Artist Group for work that stretches well beyond the stage. Deadline reported that the agency will represent her in film, television, branding, literary projects and international touring.

The new representation comes as Scott is closing out a year that put her back on the road and in the Grammy race. Scott’s business partner Shawn Gee and attorney Stephen Barnes will stay on, Deadline reported.

Scott had already spent years working both sides of that music-and-film split. She played Sheila in Tyler Perry’s Why Did I Get Married? films and spoke with Angie Martinez about the role in an interview that also covered how she got back to making an album after a decade away.

Scott starred as Ella Fitzgerald and served as an executive producer on Ella, directed by Nikki Taylor-Roberts. The film won a 2026 NAACP Image Award for live-action short form and screened at the American Black Film Festival.

Scott and Live Nation Urban announced a 36-date run in support of To Whom This May Concern, including stops in the U.S., the U.K. and continental Europe. The South African shows meant to close the run were canceled in October, with no rescheduled dates announced at the time.

“You have had time to digest the new music and now it is time to experience the full vision!” Scott wrote on her website when she announced the tour. It was the first chance to take a new Jill Scott album on the road in over a decade.

The record behind that tour is her first studio album since 2015’s Woman, and it’s now part of five Grammy nominations. Scott is up for Best R&B Album and Best Traditional R&B Performance for “Beautiful People.” “Pressha” earned her two more nominations, one for the performance and another for the song she co-wrote.

The fifth nomination came with JID for “To B Honest,” in the Grammys’ new R&B collaboration category. Scott already has three Grammys, including one with Lupe Fiasco for “Daydreamin’.” This time, it’s an Atlanta rapper joining her on a record of her own.

item.title: Saweetie’s New Songs Carry A 10K Projects Credit After Warner EP
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Saweetie's two new tracks list 10K Projects on Apple Music, a change from the ICY and Warner Records credit on her 2025 EP.
item.content:encoded:
Saweetie is releasing music under a different label credit. Her two-song single, led by “details” and backed by “in ya face,” lists 10K Projects on Apple Music. Her previous EP, HELLA PRESSURE, carried a joint ICY and Warner Records credit in 2025.

It’s a different name on the new recordings, but not a label outside the Warner orbit. Warner Music Group announced a joint venture with 10K Projects in 2023 that brought Elliot Grainge’s label into the larger company while letting it operate as a standalone label. The announcement also said 10K’s artists would get support from ADA, Warner’s global distribution arm.

Saweetie described the songs as a preview of what she wants to make next. “Throughout the years of my career I’ve learned that moving with intention and giving myself the space to evolve is where the magic happens,” she said in a statement about the singles.

She’s been public about disagreeing with her label over what listeners should hear and when. In 2024, Saweetie told fans that she’d wanted to put “Nani” out earlier, but Warner Records hadn’t signed off on the timing. She had also said the label wouldn’t clear “Icy Girl, Icy World,” a song she’d previewed for fans.

Saweetie also talked to Allure about feeling unsupported by her label. “I felt like I was left out to dry by my label and everyone around me,” she told the magazine. She also paid for the studio session, video and styling for “Immortal Freestyle” herself after Warner didn’t want her to release the song outside its schedule.

She later put five songs on HELLA PRESSURE, ranging from “boffum,” with producer J White Did It, to “superstars,” with K-pop group TWICE. In an earlier Apple Music interview, she discussed keeping creative control over her sound as she worked toward her first full-length album, then known as Pretty B#### Music.

The new two-pack is shorter, with JD Reid producing “details” and “in ya face” as the B-side. Saweetie has described the pair as a taste of what she’s making next, but the release announcement didn’t name an album or give it a date.

item.title: Jaafar Jackson Wins Hollywood Music Award For “Bad” In “Michael”
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Jaafar Jackson earns a Hollywood Music in Media Award for recreating his uncle's "Bad" performance in the biopic Michael.
item.content:encoded:
Jaafar Jackson won a Hollywood Music in Media Award for performing “Bad” in Michael, the film that marked his acting debut. The 17th annual ceremony took place November 18 at the Avalon in Hollywood.

Jackson won for onscreen song performance in a film. His fellow nominees were Julianne Moore for The Debut, Nick Jonas for Power Ballad, Linda Perry for Linda Perry: Let It Die Here, and Ethan Gold for Brother Verses Brother.

“Bad” was also the first performance Jackson filmed. Director Antoine Fuqua told The Credits that the scene put Jackson in front of hundreds of screaming extras on his first day. Getting it from every angle meant Jackson had to repeat the number over several days.

“I share the same blood as him,” he told The Envelope.

Before shooting a concert scene, Jackson had to learn how to act. He told GQ that producer Graham King first asked if he would try working with a coach.

Jackson later sent King a voice memo with his impression of Michael speaking and singing, and King set him up with acting coach Angela Gibbs.

Jackson also trained with Rich and Tone Talauega, who had worked with his uncle on the HIStory Tour. He turned part of the family’s Hayvenhurst home into a rehearsal space and used his uncle’s personal writings to help place scenes in the right period of his life.

“That day, just singing it all falsetto, the very next day my voice was gone,” Jackson said of filming. Fuqua shot in the Los Angeles recording studios that Michael had used for Off the Wall.

Fuqua also went back to the location where Michael shot the “Thriller” video. Costume designer Marci Rodgers made replicas the crew could compare with Michael’s originals. The Grammy trophies seen in the film belonged to Michael himself.

Fuqua’s film earned more than $1 billion worldwide. It follows Michael from his years with the Jackson 5 to his rise as a solo star.

The Critics Choice Association also honored Jackson for the role with its film acting award at the November 16 Celebration of Black Cinema & Television.

item.title: Teyana Taylor Takes Group Chat Dating Stories To Warner Bros.
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Teyana Taylor sells Warner Bros. a dating comedy she'll co-write, with longtime collaborator Coco Gilbert joining as producer.
item.content:encoded:
Teyana Taylor is taking dating stories from her circle to Warner Bros. The studio bought her original comedy pitch, and she’ll co-write it and produce through The Aunties. Her longtime creative partner Courtney ‘CoCo’ Gilbert will produce alongside her.

The comedy draws on Taylor’s own experiences and stories she’s collected from friends, relatives and group chats, The Hollywood Reporter reports. It’s about the mess of dating now, with women at the center of the story.

Taylor is likely to direct, according to the report. The project is in early development, with no cast or release date announced.

Taylor and Gilbert built The Aunties out of a partnership that started in music and dance. Gilbert worked as Taylor’s dance captain and creative director, and they went on to make music videos for artists including Megan Thee Stallion and Monica. “I’m a dancer, then a dance captain, then a choreographer, and now we have our own production company,” Gilbert told Red Bull.

Taylor had already been directing her own videos and paying attention to how directors ran film sets. In an interview with Allure on the set of Get Lite, she explained how different the work is once you’re responsible for every shot.

“Baby, when they yell, ‘Cut, that’s a wrap,’ you gotta stay back. You gotta come in early. You literally have to approve every single thing,” Taylor said.

Her acting roles have taken her from playing a mother trying to keep her son out of foster care in A Thousand and One to playing revolutionary Perfidia Beverly Hills in One Battle After Another. A.V. Rockwell’s A Thousand and One won the 2023 Sundance Grand Jury Prize. Taylor’s work with Paul Thomas Anderson earned her a supporting actress Oscar nomination and a Golden Globe.

The move into film hasn’t ended her recording career. She returned from a five-year break with Escape Room, then earned a Grammy nomination for the album. She directed the short film that accompanied it, too. Get Lite, her first feature as a director, follows a dance student who finds his people in the New York City subway.

Paramount’s Get Lite, which stars Storm Reid, is set for August 20, 2027.
